title: billing.payment.succeeded payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.payment.succeeded` event: a charge settled. **This type has two shapes, and the schema says so rather than flattening them.** A settled charge is either backed by an invoice (`invoice_id`, `subscription_id`, `attempt_count`, `next_payment_attempt`) or by a one-time Checkout session (`checkout_session_id`, `client_reference_id`). The `oneOf` below makes that a machine-checked fact: exactly one of the two, never both and never neither. A flat schema with every field optional would validate both shapes and let a consumer read `invoice_id` as present when it is not — see D11. **The recipient fact, added 2026-10-07 (core-w46): `email` is the customer's billing address, and it is OPTIONAL and NEVER NULL.** billing's `StripeEvents.with_recipient` merges it only when `customers.email` is present — a customer created in the processor's dashboard has no cafaye row, and one created through `/v1` has no email until the client sets one — so the field is absent, never null, and sometimes absent. Declared optional and non-nullable: required would reject every event for a customer with no address, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. `format: email` is core's convention for an address (see `billing.customer.created`). The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

oneOf.title: Invoice-backed
oneOf.description: A recurring charge: the invoice settled.

oneOf.title: Checkout-backed
oneOf.description: A one-time charge: a Checkout session in payment mode completed.

processor.description: The payment processor. Present on every billing payload: an id from a processor means nothing without knowing which processor issued it.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. Distinct on each of the two shapes: a Checkout session that completes after an invoice settles would otherwise be counted twice.

kind.description: Always `payment`. The two payment payloads share it; the three subscription payloads say `subscription`.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. Present on both shapes, and the join back to a `billing.customer.created`. It is also the envelope's `subject` whenever the payload carries no `subscription_id`, because a one-time charge belongs to no subscription.

payment_intent_id.description: The processor's payment intent, e.g. `pi_…`, or null when the charge settled without one. The closest thing both shapes have to a payment identity, which is why it is the one id required on both.

amount.description: What was collected, in integer minor units and a currency. Never a float: a Float cannot represent 0.10 and must never carry an amount. On the invoice shape this is `amount_paid`; on the Checkout shape, `amount_total`.

amount_minor.description: Amount collected in the currency's minor units. Zero is a real settled amount — a fully discounted invoice — and is not the same as absent.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase, normalised on the way in because processors differ on case.

paid.description: The processor's settled flag. Normally `true` for this type, but deliberately not constrained to it: a Checkout session can complete with an unpaid status for an asynchronous payment method, and a schema that refused it would reject a real settlement rather than a fake one.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`, on the invoice-backed shape. Always equal to the envelope's `subject` there. Absent on the Checkout-backed shape, and null when the invoice was not for a subscription — which is why the two shapes are told apart by `invoice_id` and not by this.

invoice_id.description: The processor's invoice id, e.g. `in_…`. The marker of the invoice-backed shape: present means the money is a recurring charge, absent means a one-time one.

attempt_count.description: How many times the processor had attempted this invoice, on the invoice-backed shape. Null on the Checkout-backed one. This is what tells a consumer whether a settled charge was the first try.

next_payment_attempt.description: RFC3339 UTC when the processor will retry, or null when there is nothing to retry. Null on every settled charge and populated on some `billing.payment.failed` payloads; a consumer that reads it as "the next billing date" will be wrong.

checkout_session_id.description: The processor's Checkout session id, e.g. `cs_…`. The marker of the Checkout-backed shape.

client_reference_id.description: An opaque reference the caller put on the Checkout session, on the Checkout-backed shape. It is whatever the caller chose — frequently a cafaye account id, but nothing guarantees that, so core does not type it as one.

email.description: The customer's billing email, or ABSENT — never null — when there is no address to carry. billing's `StripeEvents.with_recipient` resolves it from the processor's customer id by one indexed lookup on `customers.processor_customer_id` and merges it only when `customers.email` is present: a customer created in the processor's dashboard has no cafaye row, and one created through `/v1` has no email until the client sets one. Optional and non-nullable for that reason: required would reject every event for a customer with no address, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. Named `email` to match identity's events, which carry the same fact for the same reason — one fleet, one field name for the address a consumer cannot look up.
